steps.say: The gullet travels through the neck, the chest and a short abdominal segment before joining the stomach. Each part receives blood from its own local branches, so a surgeon freeing the oesophagus must preserve every segmental vessel. The two vagal trunks run alongside it at the hiatus and must be identified before any division.
steps.tx: The **oesophagus** (food pipe) travels in **cervical, thoracic and abdominal segments** (neck, chest and belly portions) with a **segmental blood supply** (each part fed by its own local vessels) from thyroid, bronchial, aortic, left gastric and phrenic branches. The **anterior vagus** (front trunk from the left vagus) and the **posterior vagus** (back trunk from the right vagus) run with it at the hiatus and are identified before any division.

steps.say: The lower sphincter is a short sleeve of muscle that stays contracted between swallows, and the diaphragm pinches the same spot from outside. Together they form the anti-reflux barrier. When resting pressure falls below 10 mmHg, gastric contents wash upward and the patient feels heartburn.
steps.tx: The **lower oesophageal sphincter** (muscular gate at the stomach entry) is a **3 to 4 cm** (three to four centimetre) high-pressure sleeve reinforced outside by the **crural diaphragm** (diaphragm muscle pinching the hiatus). A resting pressure below **10 mmHg** (ten millimetres of mercury) marks an incompetent barrier, so acid escapes upward and produces reflux symptoms.

steps.say: When food sticks, manometry records pressure at every level during test swallows. The Chicago version 4 scheme reads that tracing and names the disorder. A high integrated relaxation pressure proves the sphincter fails to open, which separates achalasia from other patterns.
steps.tx: Swallowing difficulty is mapped by **high-resolution manometry** (pressure sensors along the gullet). The **Chicago Classification** (manometry reporting standard) **version 4** (fourth edition) sorts tracings into **achalasia types I, II and III** (absent peristalsis patterns one to three) and **oesophagogastric junction outflow obstruction** (blocked outlet with preserved body movement), using the **integrated relaxation pressure** (mean sphincter pressure after swallowing) as the deciding number.

steps.say: Symptoms alone cannot prove reflux, so selected patients swallow a thin probe that stays in place for a full day and night. The recorder counts every acid episode against meals and posture. A DeMeester score above 14.7 confirms disease and separates it from functional heartburn.
steps.tx: Proof of reflux needs **24-hour pH-impedance monitoring** (day-long acid probe). A **DeMeester score** (composite reflux score) above **14.7** (fourteen point seven) or an **acid exposure time** (fraction of day bathed in acid) above **6 percent** (six percent) confirms pathological reflux under Lyon Consensus 2.0, excluding functional heartburn.

steps.say: The timed swallow watches barium drain under gravity and films the column at set minutes. Achalasia holds the column above a smooth tapered point, while spasm twists the lumen into coils. A column still present at five minutes proves emptying has failed.
steps.tx: The **timed barium swallow** (contrast filmed at set minutes) shows a **bird-beak** (smooth tapered point) tapering in achalasia and a **corkscrew** (coiled rosary-bead lumen) pattern in distal spasm. A retained column at **1 and 5 minutes** (one and five minutes) marks poor emptying and tracks response to myotomy or dilation.

vis.caption: Achalasia on barium swallow: dilated column-like oesophagus tapering to a bird-beak point at the junction. Credit: University of Washington Virtual Patient.

steps.say: Once cancer is found, the echoendoscope measures exactly how deep the tumour reaches through the wall layers. That depth sets the T category. The same sitting samples nodes around the celiac axis, which decides whether treatment starts with surgery or with chemotherapy.
steps.tx: **Endoscopic ultrasound** (internal echo probe staging) resolves wall layers to assign the **T category** (depth-based tumour stage) and samples **celiac nodes** (belly artery lymph glands) by **fine-needle aspiration** (needle sampling through the scope). Shallow disease stays endoscopic, locally advanced disease takes neoadjuvant therapy first, and resectable deeper tumours proceed to oesophagectomy.

steps.say: A sudden tear after vomiting is unmistakable: severe chest pain with crackling air under the skin of the neck. Listening over the chest may catch a crunching sound with each heartbeat. The first test must use a contrast agent that is safe if it leaks into the chest.
steps.tx: Forceful vomiting can burst the gullet, giving the **Mackler triad** (vomiting, chest pain and neck air) of vomiting, chest pain and subcutaneous emphysema with a **Hamman crunch** (mediastinal crackle with each heartbeat). Confirmation starts with a **water-soluble contrast** (leak-safe dye) swallow, since free barium would scar the mediastinum.

steps.say: Cutting both vagal trunks stops acid drive permanently, but it also paralyses the pumping of the lower stomach. Food would then sit and stagnate. That is why every truncal vagotomy adds a procedure that widens or bypasses the outlet.
steps.tx: **Truncal vagotomy** (division of both vagal trunks) at the hiatus abolishes acid drive but paralyses the **antral pump** (grinding motion of the lower stomach). A **pyloroplasty** (surgical widening of the outlet) or gastrojejunostomy (stomach-to-bowel bypass) must accompany it, or food stagnates above a denervated pylorus.
